meetings.title: Procurement Review
meetings.summary_text: The procurement review covered the stationery contract, the printer leases and the purchase approval limits. The group agreed to renew the stationery contract with Paper Trail for two years, since it is five percent cheaper and reliable on delivery, with Owen confirming with the supplier and Hannah checking the terms first. Hannah had already secured an extension of the four printer leases until June at the same price, so that item was settled. The approval limit for a purchase without a second quote will rise from two thousand dollars to five thousand dollars from the first of December.

meetings.title: Board Risk Committee Meeting
meetings.summary_text: The risk committee reviewed the top risks register, cyber security, supplier concentration and the budget contingency. The committee added regulatory change as a fourth top risk, and it agreed to keep the Fernwood contingency reserve ring-fenced until the forecast is reviewed. Helen will bring a plan for alternatives to the two most critical services at the next meeting, and the audit committee papers and security test summary are to be circulated in advance.

decisions.text: Regulatory change is added to the top risks register as a fourth risk.
The Fernwood contingency reserve of two million dollars remains ring-fenced until after the forecast is reviewed.

highlights.text: The penetration test found two medium findings, both fixed and retested, and the next test is scheduled for the first quarter.
Phishing click rates have halved since the last drill, and another drill is planned next quarter.
Three suppliers account for almost half of total spend.
There were no reportable incidents this quarter.
The next audit committee meets on the second Tuesday of next month.

meetings.title: Customer Success Retrospective
meetings.summary_text: The Customer Success retrospective reviewed the last quarter, covering what went well, what did not, and what to change. Response times improved and the satisfaction score rose to eighty-six percent, but onboarding delays occurred after a trainer was lost and not quickly replaced. The team agreed to contact customers at forty-five days of inactivity, after a churn review showed cancelled accounts had typically not logged in for sixty days, and to create a one-page sales handover template.

narrative.text: The Customer Success retrospective reviewed the last quarter, covering what went well, what did not, and what to change.
Response times improved and the satisfaction score rose to eighty-six percent, but onboarding delays occurred after a trainer was lost and not quickly replaced.

The team agreed to contact customers at forty-five days of inactivity, after a churn review showed cancelled accounts had typically not logged in for sixty days, and to create a one-page sales handover template.

decisions.text: Customers will be contacted at forty-five days of inactivity, before they reach sixty days.
A one-page handover template will be created and agreed with the sales team.

highlights.text: New customers waited more than two weeks for their first training session after a trainer was lost and not backfilled quickly.
The Marlin Point churn review found most cancelled accounts had not logged in for sixty days before cancelling.
Satisfaction score rose to eighty-six percent.
Sales handovers sometimes leave the team unaware of what was promised to the customer.

action_items.description: Build the inactivity report and share it
Write the call script for inactivity outreach
Write the handover template draft
Set up a meeting with the sales lead
Book the follow-up retrospective
Arrange a celebration of the improved satisfaction score with the team

meetings.title: Security Incident Debrief
meetings.summary_text: The debrief reviewed the Cobalt Reef phishing drill, in which 61 of 400 staff clicked the link and 23 entered credentials, an improvement on the previous drill but still too many. The team agreed to test an external-email banner visible on mobile devices and to send staff a reminder on reporting suspicious emails, and it agreed to plan the next drill for the middle of next quarter.

narrative.text: The debrief reviewed the Cobalt Reef phishing drill, in which 61 of 400 staff clicked the link and 23 entered credentials, an improvement on the previous drill but still too many.

The team agreed to test an external-email banner visible on mobile devices and to send staff a reminder on reporting suspicious emails, and it agreed to plan the next drill for the middle of next quarter.

decisions.text: Staff will be sent a short reminder about how to report suspicious emails, to be approved by Karim.
The next phishing drill will be planned for the middle of next quarter.

highlights.text: Ninety people reported the simulated message, and the fastest report came within four minutes.
Most people who clicked were working on mobile devices, where the sender address is harder to see.
Nobody was disciplined, so that staff feel safe reporting.

action_items.description: Test the external email banner on mobile
Draft the reminder about reporting suspicious emails and send it to Karim for approval
Report the drill results to the executive team
